<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Re-run detection for a site"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/sites/{siteId}/evaluations"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Runs the detector over every forward pick face of the site now and raises
the requests it finds. It is a sweep that converges: a pick face that
already has an open request is reported as `alreadyOpen` and left alone,
so running it twice raises nothing the second time. Requires an
`Idempotency-Key`; replaying the same key returns the original summary
with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.

  id={"request"}
  as={"h2"}
  className={"openapi-tabs__heading"}

<ParamsDetails
  parameters={[{"name":"Idempotency-Key","in":"header","required":true,"description":"Caller-generated unique key (a UUID per logical submit) that makes a\nretried request safe. The service always runs on Postgres, so it is\nrequired on every deployment and answered with 400\n`idempotency-key-required` when absent; a replay with the same key and\nthe same request (method, path and body) returns the original response\nwith the header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, while the same key with a\ndifferent request is 409 `idempotency-key-reused`. A key longer than 128\ncharacters is also 400 `idempotency-key-required`. A 2xx answer is\nstored and replayed. Of the refusals, every problem type has one\nreplay class (ADR 0014): a FINAL one (the request-shaped 400s, 404\n`replenishment-not-found`, 409 `replenishment-not-open`) is stored and\nreplayed like a success; a RETRYABLE one (`concurrent-modification`,\n`replenishment-already-open`, `no-forward-assignment`, `no-policy`,\n`no-source-stock`, `nothing-to-replenish`, `quantity-exceeds-max`) is\nnot stored and its key is released, so the same key may be sent again\nonce the cause changed, and a different body under it is a new request;\na 5xx is never stored.\n","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128}},{"name":"siteId","in":"path","required":true,"description":"The site id (the facility site code).","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":64,"pattern":"\\S"},"example":"SITE-1"}]}
>
  
</ParamsDetails>
